title: EVerest federated testing OpenHTF profile
description: The shape a normalised submission must have. OpenHTF has no published JSON Schema - its record is defined by openhtf/core/test_record.py - so this file doubles as the structural definition and as the EVerest tightening of it. Field names and enum values are taken verbatim from google/openhtf@master.

dut_id.description: Device under test. Native OpenHTF - this is the hardware identity CTRF has no field for. For SIL runs use a stable synthetic id such as sil.

station_id.description: Which station ran it. Native OpenHTF.

outcome.description: Run outcome. Verbatim OpenHTF Outcome enum - note it carries ERROR, TIMEOUT and ABORTED, which CTRF cannot express at all.

start_time_millis.description: Epoch milliseconds. Must be real: a record with no timestamp can never be aged, so the staleness rule could never govern it.

metadata.$comment: Typed as an object here and validated in full against everest-htf-metadata.schema.json. The type matters on its own: this schema runs on the document AS SUBMITTED, and it is what stops a metadata of the wrong shape reaching the code that reads it.

phases.description: OpenHTF's equivalent of CTRF tests[]. A converted CTRF submission maps each test to one phase.

outcome.description: Verbatim OpenHTF PhaseOutcome enum. Note it differs from the run-level Outcome: SKIP exists here, TIMEOUT and ABORTED do not.

measurements.description: The reason OpenHTF was chosen as the normal form. CTRF has no concept of a measurement, so a converted CTRF submission has none - that asymmetry is expected and is not an error.

attachments.description: OpenHTF inlines these as base64 by default. Capped by the gate, because the repository keeps submissions indefinitely.

codeinfo.description: Carries sourcecode, which OpenHTF includes by default. The gate WARNS if it is populated, because integrator tests may be closed source and this repository is public.

tags.description: Not native OpenHTF. Added by EVerest so per-protocol rollups survive the move from CTRF, where tags were native.
